536. Matrix Password Cracker

Problem Statement:
Smith is a professional thief and also a clever one. He breaks into a bank and tries to loot the money which is locked in highly secure lockers which are password protected digitally. Every locker contains a QR code, which on scanning, displays a square matrix of numbers on your phone. The password is hidden in plain sight in the matrix and yet can never be cracked if you don’t know the pattern in which it is stored, which is known only by the bank manager. The locker rings a burglar alarm on 2 incorrect password attempts. Smith tries a first time, to which he is greeted with an “incorrect password” message. He decides to try his luck the second time. He enters a sequence of digits and boom...the locker unlocks! What was the sequence that Smith would have entered? Check out the test case and try to decode the pattern.
input_spec: Dimensions of the matrix followed by the elements of the matrix
output_spec: The sequence of numbers which unlocks the locker.
